To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

motion-contamination of data can be corrected by modeling motion information in the system matrix of an EM-based iterative reconstruction method, and that the effect of the motion-contamination of attenuation factors can also be accounted for by the system matrix.

1) motion compensation of attenuation factors is required in order to avoid degradation of reconstructed images; 2) a motion-compensated reconstruction algorithm can be developed by incorporating the motion information into the emission system matrix; 3) motion-contaminated emission data can be reconstructed with high accuracy by applying the proposed algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a system matrix modeling approach to compensate for motion in the reconstruction task.
modeling the effects of motion on the system matrix of an EM reconstruction algorithm.

a new approach to motion compensation in emission tomography imaging that can be used in conjunction with any scanner in the market, and that can be implemented on a standard scanner without the need for any hardware modifications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of any other means to deal with motion, this approach can be used for reconstruction of motion-contamined data in any scanner in the clinical field.
the system matrix of an emission tomography scanner, when used in a reconstruction algorithm, should be modified to incorporate the motion information.
, for the purpose of motion compensation, the attenuation factors should be modeled in a way that they are dependent on time and position of the patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a system matrix modeling approach for motion-compensation, which can be applied to any scanner without list mode capability.
the motion information is modeled as the motion-contaminated attenuation factors in the system matrix.
the proposed approach is capable to reconstruct images of high quality, even from data acquired during patient motion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the system matrix should be modified by incorporating the motion information and the attenuation factors should be corrected for motion-contamination.
the motion information is a valuable source of information for improving image quality and should be exploited.
motion compensation can be performed in any EM-based reconstruction, provided that the system matrix is modified appropriately.
